name: Jethro
summary: A priest of Midian, called Reuel when Moses first meets his daughters at the well. He gave Moses his daughter Zipporah and his flocks to keep. After the exodus he brought Zipporah and her sons to Moses at the mountain of God, rejoiced at what the LORD had done and offered sacrifices, and advised Moses to appoint judges so as not to wear himself out.
body: Moses, a fugitive from Egypt, drives off shepherds who are keeping Reuel's seven daughters from the well. Reuel asks why they left the man behind, invites him to eat, and gives him Zipporah. Moses is keeping Jethro's flock when he comes to the burning bush, and asks Jethro's leave to return to Egypt.

Hearing all that God has done, Jethro comes to the camp and says, “Now I know that the LORD is greater than all other gods.” Watching Moses judge the people from morning till evening, he tells him, “What you are doing is not good,” and advises capable, trustworthy men over thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens. Moses does so, and Jethro goes home.

later.text: Numbers 10:29 speaks of “Hobab son of Reuel the Midianite, Moses' father-in-law,” and Judges 4:11 calls Hobab himself Moses' father-in-law. Rashi takes Hobab to be Jethro, from Judges 4:11, one of his seven names, and gives two views of Reuel: another of his names, or his father, Zipporah's grandfather, called her father as children call a grandfather (the Sifrei). Keil takes Reuel and Jethro to be one man and Hobab his son, Moses' brother-in-law, since the Hebrew ḥōtēn, like the Greek γαμβρός, can mean either; he cites the Targumists for the grandfather reading and sets aside Ranke's, that Jethro and Hobab were both Reuel's sons.

sources.title: Rashi on Exodus 18:1
sources.note: tr. Rosenbaum and Silbermann: 'He was called by seven names: Reuel, Jether, Jethro, Hobab, Heber, Keni and Putiel … Hobab is certainly identical with Jethro'

sources.title: Biblical Commentary on the Old Testament: The Pentateuch, on Exodus 2:16–18
sources.author: C. F. Keil (Keil and Delitzsch)
sources.note: 'it would probably be more correct to regard Chobab as Moses' brother-in-law, Reguel as the proper name of his father-in-law, and Jethro … as either a title, or the surname'

traditions: Jethro and Hobab one man, Reuel the same or his father: Rashi, after the Sifrei
Reuel the grandfather: the Targumists, as Keil reports them
Reuel is Jethro, Hobab his son: C. F. Keil
Jethro and Hobab brothers, both Reuel's sons: Ranke, as Keil reports him
